question: According to the regulation of the Indus Water Treaty signed in 1960, India can use only ______ of the total water carried by the Indus River system.
solution:
The correct answer is **__20%__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Indus Water Treaty** signed in **1960**, India can use only **0.2** of the total water carried by the **Indus River system.**
 
• The treaty was** brokered by the World Bank** and is considered one of the **most successful water-sharing agreements in the world.**
 
• The Indus River system comprises six rivers:** the Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.**
 
• The** treaty allocates the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej) **to India for unrestricted use, while the **western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab) are allocated to Pakistan**, with limited use by India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The treaty has survived multiple conflicts between the two countries and is a critical component of their bilateral relations.
 
• India is allowed to use the water for domestic, non-consumptive, and agricultural purposes, as well as for generating hydroelectric power, as long as it does not affect the flow to Pakistan.
 
• Regular meetings of the Permanent Indus Commission, established by the treaty, help address disputes and ensure cooperation between the two countries.
 
• The Indus Water Treaty is often cited as a model for resolving international water disputes.
